links.title: Parallax: Parameterized Local Linear Attention for Language Modeling

primary_link.title: Parallax: Parameterized Local Linear Attention for Language Modeling

papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become the central paradigm in artificial intelligence, yet the core computational primitive of attention has remained structurally unchanged. Local Linear Attention (LLA) is an attention mechanism derived from nonparametric statistics in the test-time regression framework. In contrast to prior research on efficient attention variants, LLA upgrades the local constant estimate in softmax attention to a local linear estimate, yielding provably superior bias-variance tradeoffs for associative memory. However, LLA has not been scaled in LLM pretraining due to computational and numerical stability concerns. We introduce Parallax, a parameterized Local Linear Attention that is scalable for LLMs. Parallax eliminates the numerical solver in LLA and learns an extra query-like projector that probes the KV covariance. We place Parallax within a family of attention mechanisms connected by the bandwidth, the probe construction and the affine structure. We propose a hardware-aware algorithm that increases the arithmetic intensity over FlashAttention, shifting attention into a more compute bound regime. Our prototype decode kernel matches or outperforms FlashAttention 2/3 across diverse batch sizes and context lengths. We pretrain Parallax at 0.6B and 1.7B scales and find consistent perplexity improvements throughout pretraining with gains that transfer to downstream benchmarks. The advantage persists under both parameter-matched and compute-matched controls, demonstrating a Pareto improvement. We perform careful pretraining ablations and identify a novel phenomenon whereby Muon unlocks the capacity of Parallax. To our knowledge, this is the first empirical demonstration of strong architecture-optimizer codesign for attention mechanisms in the architecture research literature.

links.title: PRISM: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Peer Reviewers

primary_link.title: PRISM: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Peer Reviewers

papers.summary: The rapid growth in submissions to machine learning venues has strained the scientific peer-review system and intensified interest in LLM-based automated peer reviewers. However, how good these systems are actually, especially compared to human reviewers at catching scientific gaps, remains poorly understood. In this work, we introduce PRISM (Peer Review Intelligence via Structured Multi-dimensional assessment), a benchmarking framework that evaluates review quality across four dimensions: Depth of Analysis, Novelty Assessment,Flaw Identification & Major Issues Prioritization, and Multi-dimensional Constructiveness. Unlike most existing evaluations based on surface-level metrics like ROUGE and BLEU, or unconstrained LLM-as-a-judge prompting that conflates fluency with rigor, PRISM grounds each dimension in argument mining, retrieval-augmented verification, and consensus-based scoring. We apply PRISM to benchmark five leading automated reviewer systems and human reviewers on a stratified corpus of reviews from ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS. The results reveal that LLMs can match or beat human reviewers on individual dimensions: comparable depth of analysis, stronger novelty verification, and highly accurate critique prioritization. However, no single system consistently matches the balanced performance of the human baseline across all dimensions at once. Each exhibits a distinct specialization profile with characteristic blind spots -- failure modes that aggregate metrics miss entirely. The implication is that LLM reviewers are best understood as targeted supplements to human review, effective within specific dimensions, but unreliable as standalone replacements. Our demo and key results can be found at https://khanhthanhdev.github.io/prism-page/.

papers.title_zh: 有秘密？LLM 代理人守不住：評估多代理人系統中的隱私

papers.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems have become the dominant production workload, but the serving stack was not built for them. radar.summary_zh: 加密浮水印是歸因於大型語言模型 (LLM) 生成文本的一項主要防禦機制。然而，現有的方案，包括 KGW、Unigram 和 DipMark，其安全性保證皆建立在底層偽隨機數生成器 (PRNG) 可信賴的假設之上。本研究引入了 SeedHijack，這是首個針對 LLM 浮水印的供應鏈攻擊，其特點是同時具備「盲性」——無需知曉浮水印密鑰、檢測器或模型 logits，並能保持文本完整性，使其難以被檢測。這項工作揭示了當前浮水印技術的關鍵安全漏洞，強調了 PRNG 在 LLM 安全生態系統中的核心脆弱性。

radar.title_zh: 盲性 PRNG 劫持：針對 LLM 浮水印的不可檢測且保持完整性的攻擊

links.title: JECA^2: Judgment-Explanation Consistent Adversarial Attack against Forensic Vision-Language Models

primary_link.title: JECA^2: Judgment-Explanation Consistent Adversarial Attack against Forensic Vision-Language Models

radar.summary_zh: 鑑識視覺語言模型 (VLMs) 近來已發展出用於偵測圖像篡改並提供自然語言解釋的能力。然而，這些模型面對對抗性操作時的魯棒性仍未被充分探索。現有的對抗性攻擊通常旨在推翻模型的二元判斷，但其伴隨的解釋可能仍會洩漏鑑識線索，並與被攻擊的判斷產生矛盾。本文深入研究了針對鑑識 VLMs 的判斷與解釋一致性對抗性攻擊，提出了 JECA^2。這項工作旨在設計一種新型攻擊，不僅能改變模型的最終判斷，還能確保模型生成的解釋與被操縱的判斷保持一致，從而更有效地規避鑑識系統，揭示了此類模型的深層安全隱患。

radar.title_zh: JECA^2：針對鑑識視覺語言模型的判斷與解釋一致性對抗性攻擊

links.title: Technical Report: Exploring the Emerging Threats of the Agent Skill Ecosystem

links.title: Semantic Optimal Transport for Sparse Autoencoder Feature Matching and Circuit Compression

radar.title_zh: 稀疏自編碼器特徵匹配與電路壓縮的語義最佳傳輸

radar.title_zh: 針對 LLM 生成程式碼片段的高效可擴展來源追蹤

links.title: RUBRIC-ARROW: Alternating Pointwise Rubric Reward Modeling for LLM Post-training in Non-verifiable Domains

primary_link.title: RUBRIC-ARROW: Alternating Pointwise Rubric Reward Modeling for LLM Post-training in Non-verifiable Domains

top5.summary: Pointwise reward modeling offers critical signals for LLM post-training, yet struggles with absolute scoring in subjective, non-verifiable settings. Rubric-based methods address this by decomposing evaluation into explicit criteria, but existing approaches typically depend on frontier LLMs and suffer from ties caused by hard Boolean aggregation. We present RUBRIC-ARROW, an alternating framework that jointly trains a rubric generator and a rubric-conditioned judge, with its RL stage using only pairwise preference data. Our method couples a probability-based scoring rule that reduces ties with phase-specific preference-based rewards and an alternating GRPO scheme that together train the pointwise evaluator. Extensive experiments show that RUBRIC-ARROW achieves competitive reward-modeling accuracy and yields consistent gains for downstream policy post-training.
top5.summary_zh: 針對主觀、不可驗證領域中 LLM 後訓練的挑戰，傳統逐點獎勵建模難以提供精確的絕對分數，而現有基於評分標準（rubric-based）的方法則常依賴於頂級 LLM 且受限於布林聚合造成的評分綁定問題。為此，本文提出了 RUBRIC-ARROW 框架，這是一個交替訓練評分標準生成器和評分標準條件判斷器的模型，其強化學習階段僅使用配對偏好資料。該方法結合了減少綁定的機率式評分規則、階段性偏好獎勵以及交替 GRPO 方案，共同訓練逐點評估器。實驗證明，RUBRIC-ARROW 在獎勵建模準確性方面表現出色，並為下游策略的後訓練帶來顯著提升。

top5.summary_zh: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting 顯著提升了 Transformer 的樣本效率，例如將奇偶性學習等任務的複雜度從輸入長度的指數級降低到多項式級。然而，在推論階段生成明確的推理步驟代價高昂。Implicit Chain-of-Thought (ICoT) 作為一種有前景的經驗性解決方案應運而生，它訓練模型將中間步驟內化到其隱藏狀態中，但其理論基礎一直未能被充分理解。本文透過嚴謹的分析，首次從理論上證明了 Transformer 能夠學習並內化 CoT，這不僅深化了對 ICoT 機制的理解，也為 Transformer 的推理能力提供了重要的理論支持。
